items.title: George Wein — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Sonny Rollins had a set the other night in New Orleans... You have to respect the other musicians.

ctx.x: I did and it was a mistake. (laughs) That's when you learn when you've got two horns that want to play and play. Sonny Rollins had a set the other night in New Orleans. He had ninety minutes. He was so involved, the people were cheering and yelling, and he came off the stage and he was in another world. He didn't know where he was, he was so taken ….. He didn't stop playing that horn for ninety minutes but he had enough time – he didn't go overtime. But if he had been doing an hour set, he would have gone over…
'56. He said, "I'm not gonna play exit music." So you see there are many things to think about. And you learn as you go along.
